items.q: MiniMax already had a 10 million token window. Why bring 1 million back?
items.a: M1/01 could **dump a book and review it**. That model was **not agentic**. Once the agent talks to the environment — **tool results, multi-round traces** — a short window dies. They brought **functional 1M context back for agents**.

items.q: How is a million tokens cheap enough to ship?
items.a: **MiniMax Sparse Attention**: an **index branch** picks the blocks that matter; a **sparse branch** attends only there. An **intern** designed it. Flash Attention had paused linear-attention research; this is first-principles attention again.

items.q: Why train vision from step one instead of bolting it on?
items.a: **Adapters after text hurt language** and vision converges poorly. Mid-train is **recipe-fragile** and does not scale. They **interleave real images and video**, work the ViT, and avoid the usual **collapse**.

items.q: What agent jobs does native video unlock?
items.a: Read an unstructured **PowerPoint**, watch a **long video**, then **act with tools**. Wolf: the agent finally watches your YouTube tutorial. Harness support is still the gap.

sections.title: Lab culture and the next model

items.q: How does MiniMax pick the next research bet?
items.a: After a ship, **anyone can play, invent evals, find a weakness, and propose**. Others join for weeks or months. What works goes into the **next train**. Hugging Face **PRs and failure reports** feed later versions.

No. **M3.1.** Internal **research harnesses** automate kernel work, model-on-model, and auto data. Song's excitement next: **multi-agents + model routing** — more complex tasks, and a diagnostic of what models cannot do.
